evidence: Eq1/C constructs a within-rollout late-minus-early mean direction; the landmark uses future gold-first-token probability stabilization, not a deployable correctness signal. The paper discloses same problems on both readout splits.

Section4/Table17 shows strong steering alone can greatly reduce accuracy. Successful headline results require per-problem gold-answerable training targets and full-vector LoRA reconstruction (Eq4-5), not simple addition of the published halt direction.
Section5/Table7 held steering beats tent schedule in the trained adapter. This is not evidence that holding the existing ReBalance reflection vector throughout each step will preserve accuracy.
Section6.6/Table3 compares sampled self-halt with greedy DEER against separate anchors; these are not identical-decoding head-to-head results.
AppendixD says all rows16k but Table18 explicitly labels12288 as the cap; Table17 has8192-valued cells and the official steer_scan default is12288. Do not copy its cap into current experiments.

AppendixC calls layer0 embedding, but value_axis_core.py:27-33 drops hidden_states[0] and uses hidden_states[1:], making returned index0 decoder0 output. The layer0-as-embedding argument does not match this public implementation.

Eq3 prose describes reference mean norm; steer_scan.py:157-169 recalculates current-call h.norm().mean(), while train_reptarget.py:239-257 computes a frozen dataset reference. Record the difference when translating actuation.

AppendixC says457 usable contrasts and also457 held-out rollouts; build_value_axis.py:199-204 allocates each item to construct/heldout by a mod3 rule. Without released raw volume data the actual held-out count is unverified.
